newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonia's Tallinna eyes Latvian bank.
newsitem.headline: Estonia's Tallinna eyes Latvian bank.

text.p: One of Estonia's leading banks Tallinna Pank on Thursday said it intended to buy a bank in neighbouring Latvia, Saules Bank.
The Estonians, seen as having the most advanced banking market of the Baltic states, have been making the running in cross-border expansion.
The country's largest bank, Hansapank, already has bank operations in Latvia.
Tallinna, Estonia's fourth largest bank, already owns 20 percent of Saules.
"We plan to increase our stake...to 100 percent," Raus told a news conference.
However, Saules Bank said it had no information on Tallinna Pank's intentions.
Tallinna Pank later made an official statement to the bourse, confirming its plans for Latvia.
"Tallinna Pank sees in its short-term strategy a possible merger with Saules Banka," it said in a statement.
Raus said he would not say anything on the conditions for any agreement as negotiations were still going on.
He said the goal was to reach an agreement by the end of this year.
"We think Saules is the best partner in the Latvian market and the most favourable for us," Raus said.
Raus said Tallinna Pank saw itself as a universal bank in the whole of the Baltics.
It also plans to start banking activities in third Baltic state Lithuania but no decisions have been made yet.
